fire: The many-worlds interpretation, defended by Everett, DeWitt and Deutsch, denies that the wavefunction ever collapses.
Bell's theorem shows that no local hidden-variable theory can reproduce the predictions of quantum mechanics.
Substantivalists hold that spacetime exists independently of the matter it contains.
Whether simultaneity is a matter of convention was debated by Reichenbach and Grünbaum.
The measurement problem asks why observations yield definite outcomes if the wavefunction evolves linearly.
Relationalists such as Leibniz argued that space is nothing over and above the relations among bodies.
In the Copenhagen interpretation, Bohr insisted that quantum phenomena must be described in classical terms.
Einstein, Podolsky and Rosen argued that quantum mechanics gives an incomplete description of reality.
